subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw core expose persisted per-cron lifecycle hooks that can run shell or webhook actions, and what trust boundary/API should own that behavior?
rationale: The remaining work defines public cron config/protocol behavior and can execute unattended commands or outbound calls, which requires maintainer product and security intent rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Approve a narrow core hook API
options.body: Define an additive CronJob hook/gate contract with explicit command/webhook permissions, phases, failure semantics, upgrade-safe docs, and coverage across all cron execution paths.

options.title: Route hooks to plugins or ClawHub
options.body: Declare command cron plus plugin hooks as the supported path and document the external pattern instead of adding persisted CronJob.hooks to core.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave the issue open as an acknowledged gap until maintainers are ready to own the API and trust model.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core hook API
recommendation.body: Define an additive CronJob hook/gate contract with explicit command/webhook permissions, phases, failure semantics, upgrade-safe docs, and coverage across all cron execution paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current routing signal from the prior issue review plus recent cron protocol/status work.
